newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid market quiet as crude prices tumble.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid market quiet as crude prices tumble.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil market was at a near standstill Wednesday as the domestic oil market saw the benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude tumbled to its lowest price level in a more than a year.
NYMEX May crude futures settled down 81 cents at $19.47 a barrel on concerns over rising imports from Europe, West Africa and South America.
"The drop in crude had an effect on the swaps, but the physicals were quiet," said one East Coast resid trader.
Light spot demand continued to underpin the dearth of activity in the resid market, market sources said.
Barge traffic on the Mississippi River continued to be restricted amid efforts to clean up a petrochemical spill after a barge carrying the toxic material capsized March 17.
USG three percent sulphur grade softened to $13.50-14.00 per barrel from Tuesday's $13.75-14.00. One percent physical was held at $14.75-15.00.
USG three percent paper for the balance of April fell to $13.10-30 from $13.20-40 yesterday.
In the New York harbor, one percent physical remained at $15.50-75, while two sellers were heard still offering supplies at $15.50.
One percent NYH paper for rest of April was assessed at $15.00-15.10, down from Tuesday's $15.15-15.30.
NYH HSFO prices were stable with three percent staying at $13.50-75.

Swing gas deliveries at New York City gate for Thursday firmed to $2.18-2.20 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) or $13.80 a barrel equivalent from $2.15-2.20 per mmBtu or $13.67/bbl equivalent.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell to $1.85/mmBtu or 11.65/bbl equivalent from Tuesday's $1.94/mmBtu or $12.22/bbl equivalent.
